question_text:
Using the data for aluminum in  table 3.1 , compute the interplanar spacing for the (110) set of planes.


"Table 3.1
Atomic Radii and Crystal Structures for 16 Metals
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Metal & Crystal Structure ${ }^a$ & Atomic Radius ${ }^{\text {b }}$ (nm) & Metal & Crystal Structure & Atomic Radius (nm) \\
\hline Aluminum & FCC & 0.1431 & Molybdenum & BCC & 0.1363 \\
\hline Cadmium & HCP & 0.1490 & Nickel & FCC & 0.1246 \\
\hline Chromium & BCC & 0.1249 & Platinum & FCC & 0.1387 \\
\hline Cobalt & HCP & 0.1253 & Silver & FCC & 0.1445 \\
\hline Copper & FCC & 0.1278 & Tantalum & BCC & 0.1430 \\
\hline Gold & FCC & 0.1442 & Titanium ( $\alpha$ ) & HCP & 0.1445 \\
\hline Iron ( $\alpha$ ) & BCC & 0.1241 & Tungsten & BCC & 0.1371 \\
\hline Lead & FCC & 0.1750 & Zinc & HCP & 0.1332 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
${ }^a$ FCC $=$ face-centered cubic; HCP $=$ hexagonal close-packed; $\mathrm{BCC}=$ body-centered cubic. ${ }^b \mathrm{~A}$ nanometer (nm) equals $10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}$; to convert from nanometers to angstrom units ( $\AA$ ), multiply the nanometer value by 10 ."The unit of the answer is nm.
response:
For FCC aluminum:

- **Lattice parameter:** $a = 2R\sqrt{2} = 2(0.1431)\sqrt{2}$ nm
- **Interplanar spacing** for $(hkl)=(110)$:

$$d_{110} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2+l^2}} = \frac{2R\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1^2+1^2+0^2}} = \frac{2R\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 2R$$

$$d_{110} = 2(0.1431) = 0.2862 \text{ nm}$$

$$\boxed{0.2862}$$
